name: Tabletop games and role-play
description: Dice, odds, initiative, character sheets and campaign notes for tabletop and role-playing games.
note: This is a tabletop-games project: campaigns, characters, encounters and house rules for tabletop and role-playing games. The campaign notes and the group's rules are the source of truth: never invent a rule, a stat, a rule-book page, an NPC's past or a decision the players made, and say which edition or house rule you assumed. Dice are fair chance: never fudge a result, and when asked to roll use the Tabletop helper with a seed so the roll can be repeated and shown. The tool knows no game system: required fields, ability limits and point-buy costs are the ones the user passes, so ask for them. Mark clearly what is canon (already played) and what is a draft idea; keep secrets the game master has not revealed out of anything meant for players. Use only rule text the user supplies or the group has permission to use; do not reproduce publisher rule books. Keep notes in markdown, one file per session, and keep the user's originals untouched.
details: Running and playing tabletop games from plain files. The Tabletop helper tool rolls dice expressions such as 2d6+3, 4d6kh3 (keep highest), 2d20kl1 or 3d8dl1 (drop lowest) with a seed so the rolls can be repeated; gives the exact probability table of an expression with the chance of reaching a target; turns a combatants CSV into an initiative order and a round tracker (numbered copies for groups); checks a character sheet against the required fields, ability limits and point-buy table and budget that you define; and indexes your campaign notes by NPC and location so you can see where each appears and which never did. No game system or rule text is built in.
examples: What are my chances of rolling 15 or more with advantage?
Roll initiative for the party and four goblins
Check this character sheet against our 27-point budget
Which NPCs have I not used in any session yet?
